items.title: The check-in page has no Save button any more
items.why: 2.8.1's “Quick add” rename caused this. The only way to save a check-in is the centre button, which now opens the menu, where “Save check-in” is the first item. Other pages whose main action lived in the centre button have the same gap.

options.label: A Save button at the bottom of the page
options.desc: On the check-in and on every page whose main action was the centre button. Quick add stays as it is.

options.label: The centre button turns into “Save” on those pages
options.desc: Quick add everywhere else. One tap saves, as before 2.8.1.

items.title: The St. John's wort + warfarin warning never says what happens
items.why: It shows only “Warfarin, an anticoagulant (blood thinner)”. NIH's sentence that explains it (“can weaken the effects of many medicines”) is in the data but not shown. Every medicine on that list looks the same.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Show NIH's lead-in sentence above the matched medicine, word for word.

items.title: Readiness still says “Good to go” after a pain or dizzy “yes”
items.why: Answering yes to back pain when arching, pain changing a skill, or feeling dizzy shows the reminder to tell a parent and doctor, but the readiness line still reads “Readiness 84 · Good to go”.

options.label: Any “yes” changes the verdict
options.desc: The line reads “Talk to a parent or coach before training” instead of “Good to go”. The number stays.

options.label: Any “yes” also lowers the number
options.desc: Same message, and the score drops so the power level and recap reflect it.

items.title: Teen profiles are offered “Lose fat” and start with waist tracking on
items.why: “Lose fat” is a goal choice for under-18s on Strength and Custom profiles. A new Gymnastics profile starts with Symptom check-ins on, which include morning and evening waist measurements.

options.label: Hide “Lose fat” and start waist tracking off for under-18s
options.desc: Both can still be turned on in Settings by choice.

items.title: “New record” pops up and beeps on every rep
items.why: Once you pass your best, each extra rep counts as another new record, so the toast and beep repeat every rep. On a laptop the toast also covers “Drop to flat”.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: One “New record” per set, shown when you finish the set, placed where it covers nothing.

items.title: The weight buttons stay on screen during rest
items.why: During rest the “− 5 lb +” row still shows the last exercise's weight, and tapping it does nothing. A style rule overrides the code that hides it.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Hide the weight row during rest, as intended.

items.title: Holding Finish with a mouse opens two “Finish session?” dialogs
items.why: With a mouse, a long hold fires both the hold timer and the click. After Discard, a second dialog stays over Home. Touch screens are fine.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: A hold opens the dialog once.

items.title: After typing a search, the first tap on Add does nothing
items.why: Typing “bench press” then tapping Add only closes the keyboard; a second tap adds it. The list redraws as the keyboard closes.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: The first tap adds.

items.title: A logged gymnastics activity still says “Rest day”
items.why: Logging Activity → Gymnastics, 120 minutes on a planned rest day: Ki says Training done, but the Today card says “Rest day. Rest is part of training.” and the week strip gets no star. Only “sessions” count there, and Quick add only offers Activity.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Count a logged activity as training on the Today card and the week strip.

items.title: Changing time zone moves today's entries into the future
items.why: Switching New York → Honolulu made “today” Sunday. Monday's workout and food then sat in the future: power level, streak and Ki read 0, while “This week” still counted the session.

options.label: A time-zone change starts at the next day
options.desc: Today keeps its date; tomorrow follows the new zone. Good for travel.

options.label: Keep it, but warn first
options.desc: “Today's entries will show as Monday, which is now tomorrow.”

items.title: Choosing your own photo in setup fails
items.why: The code that handles the photo refers to something that doesn't exist, so it would show “t is not defined”. Found in the code; not tried with a real photo.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Fix the code so the photo is used.

items.title: Restaurant items show a made-up weight and “McDonald's's”
items.why: A Big Mac says “100 g in all” (a real one is about 220 g): the chains publish servings, not weights, and 100 was a placeholder. 125 source lines read “McDonald's's”, “Wendy's's” or “Dunkin''s”.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Show only “1 sandwich” unless the chain publishes a weight, and fix the source lines.

items.title: Searching “big mac” shows a USDA “Mac Jr” first
items.why: The first hit is USDA's “Big Mac (McDonalds)” whose serving is a Mac Jr at 352 kcal, above McDonald's own 580 kcal Big Mac. Some brand rows show unit codes like “2 ONZ” and “20 Z”.

options.label: Chain items first, readable units
options.desc: A chain's own item ranks above copies of its name. Unreadable unit codes show as grams.

items.title: “2 slices pizza”, “3 eggs” and “Chipotle bowl” miss
items.why: A leading amount stops the match (“2 slices pizza” finds nothing; “3 eggs” finds egg bites). “Chipotle bowl” finds packaged bowls, not Chipotle's 25 items. “creatine” finds an energy drink.

options.label: Smarter matching
options.desc: Ignore a leading amount (and use it as the amount), match a chain by its name, and point “creatine” to Supplements.

items.title: Back mid-workout: the button says “Leave Goku”
items.why: The dialog is titled “Leave the workout?” but its button closes the whole app, which is easy to misread.

options.label: Call it what it does
options.desc: Title “Close Goku?”, text “Your workout stays saved and picks up where you left off.”, button “Close Goku”.

items.title: Adding an exercise in Edit session adds it to your Library at once
items.why: Even if you close Edit session without saving, the exercise stays in your Library.

options.label: Add it to the Library only when you tap Save changes

items.title: Library section names don't match New exercise's 7 groups
items.why: New exercise now offers the picker's 7 groups, but the Library still shows “Power” and “Joints”. A Cardio exercise lands under Power.

options.label: Use the picker's names
options.desc: Push (chest, shoulders, triceps) … Jumps, power and cardio · Mobility and stretching.

items.title: Custom profiles get every goal idea, whatever their sports
items.why: A soccer and running profile is offered “Land my round-off back handspring”, “Full splits” and “5 pull-ups”, and no running goals.

options.label: Ideas from the sports you picked
options.desc: e.g. running: “Run 5 km without stopping”; soccer: “Juggle 50 in a row”; strength: the current strength ideas. I'd show you the full lists before adding them.

items.title: The weight buttons always use your dumbbell step
items.why: + and − use the dumbbell step (5 lb) for every exercise, barbell and machines included.

options.label: Barbell and machines step by 5 lb (2.5 kg)
options.desc: Dumbbells keep your own step from Settings.

items.title: “Why?” still does the math in kg for pound users
items.why: The card says “0.64–0.91 g per lb”, but Why? shows “83.9 kg × 1.4 g = 117 g”. Rounding differs (1.36 vs 1.4), and one line has doubled brackets.

options.label: Do the math in lb for pound users
options.desc: e.g. “185 lb × 0.64 g = 117 g”, with one rounding rule everywhere.

items.title: Protein goal is the bottom of the range, and nothing says why
items.why: With “Build muscle” picked at 185 lb, Home aims for 117 g, the bottom of 1.4–2.0 g per kg. The goal you picked isn't used, and Why? doesn't say the bottom is the target.

options.label: Explain it
options.desc: Why? says “Home aims for the bottom of the range; reach it most days.”

options.label: “Build muscle” aims for the middle
options.desc: About 1.7 g per kg (still inside the ISSN range); others stay at the bottom.

items.title: Past days still say “today”
items.why: On an earlier day: “calories today”, “None logged today”, “Tap + Food to start the day”. The Add food sheet doesn't say which day it adds to.

options.label: Name the day
options.desc: “calories on Sun, Nov 1”, and Add food shows “Adding to Sun, Nov 1”.

items.title: Egg offers “1 slice”, and Banana appears twice
items.why: “Egg, boiled” lists 1 egg / 1 cup / 1 slice. “Banana 122 kcal” and “Bananas, raw 105 kcal” both show.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Drop servings that don't fit and keep one banana (USDA's medium banana).

items.title: Magnesium with levothyroxine isn't flagged
items.why: Goku's copy of NIH's Magnesium sheet (March 2021) doesn't list thyroid medicine, so this matches the data. NIH may have updated the sheet.

options.label: Re-read NIH's current sheet
options.desc: Add it only if NIH lists it, with the date. I won't add anything NIH doesn't say.

items.title: Height and weight errors can hide below the keyboard
items.why: With the keyboard up, “That height doesn't look right” sits off screen, and only the first problem shows (a bad weight appears only after fixing the height).

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Scroll the error into view and list every problem at once.

items.title: The Interaction check opens on Close
items.why: Typing a medicine and pressing Enter closes the sheet, because the cursor starts on Close.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Open with the cursor in the medicine box.

items.title: The calendar's “Senzu save” key wraps on a phone
items.why: The dot sits at the end of one line and its word starts the next.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Keep each dot with its word.

items.title: Log activity starts on Soccer for a gymnastics profile
items.why: Only Custom profiles start on their own sport.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Start on Gymnastics.

items.title: Four small wording slips
items.why: Coach says “tap Skip” but the button is “Not now”. History says “1 sets”. The rest-day hint says “quick menu” (now Quick add). Finish's screen-reader label says “hold to charge”.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Correct all four.

items.title: A matched supplement also says “Not in Goku's list”
items.why: Searching beetroot, AG1, greens, LMNT or whey shows the match and, under it, “Add “beetroot”: Not in Goku's list.”

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Hide that row when something matched.

items.title: Search hints that aren't words
items.why: “GU gel” suggests “gu gelato / gu gelat / gu gela”.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Only suggest whole words from the food list.

items.title: Three screen-reader slips
items.why: The calendar key is hidden from screen readers, New exercise is announced as “Edit exercise”, and “Enter the same 6 digits again” stays announced after setup.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Fix all three.

items.title: Link text is too faint on some backgrounds
items.why: Accent links are checked against cards only. On the page background they measure 4.25:1 and on lavender panels 3.88:1 (the guideline is 4.5:1). Seen in Encore light.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Check links against every background and darken where needed.

items.title: A 24-character name pushes Settings sideways
items.why: In Settings → Profiles the row is wider than the phone, so the page scrolls sideways. The name chip at the top cuts the name off without “…”.

options.label: Fix it
options.desc: Shorten long names with “…” in both places.

items.title: Back during first-time setup leaves the app
items.why: First-time setup has no Cancel, so Back closes the app and the answers are lost.

options.label: Back goes to the previous setup step

items.title: Power level and “This week” count different weeks
items.why: Power level uses the last 7 days; “This week” uses Sunday to Saturday, side by side.

options.label: Label it “last 7 days” on the power level

items.title: With two profiles, one tap on the name switches at once
items.why: There's no picker, so “Add a profile” is only in Settings.

options.label: Keep one-tap switching
options.desc: Fast for two people sharing the phone; Add a profile stays in Settings.

options.label: Tap opens a small picker
options.desc: Switch or Add a profile; one extra tap to switch.

items.title: Dragon Ball characters appear in Encore and Plain
items.why: The avatar step lists Fighters (Goku, Vegeta, Frieza…) in every skin, first in Plain. Auras are named “Saiyan gold”, “Namekian green”, “Majin pink”.

options.label: Hide Fighters in Encore and Plain, plain aura names
options.desc: “Gold”, “Green”, “Pink” there. Dragon Ball keeps everything.

options.label: Keep Fighters, but list them last

items.title: More Dragon Ball words left in Encore and Plain
items.why: Saga: “Your saga”, “ARC 1 CLEARED”, “Boss defeated”, name ideas “Gravity training”, “Skill saga”. Elsewhere: “How much ki do you have today?”, “starting gravity level”, “Today's scouter”, “First power level record”, “All seven Dragon Balls”.

options.label: Use each skin's words everywhere
options.desc: Dragon Ball stays the same.

items.title: Theme names are Dragon Ball places in every skin
items.why: Settings lists Namek, Super Saiyan, Time Chamber and Kame House in Encore and Plain too.

options.label: Plain names in Encore and Plain
options.desc: e.g. Green, Gold, Night, Beach. Same colors.

items.title: Encore calls gravity “volume”
items.why: Screens read “×100 volume” and “Change volume”, but “volume” already means amount of training.

options.label: “intensity”
options.desc: Same as Plain.

options.label: “energy”
options.desc: “×100 energy”, “Change energy”.

items.title: Encore's words together may suggest one real tour
items.why: There's no name, lyric or album art. But Era + Tour + friendship bracelets + Showstopper + The encore together point strongly at one artist's tour. Your family's call.

options.label: Keep the words
options.desc: The Encore profile's owner picked the pop-tour feel.

options.label: Swap two words
options.desc: “Era” → “Chapter”, “friendship bracelet” → “charm”. Keeps the pop-tour feel.

items.title: Weight × reps history per exercise
items.why: A chart of weight and reps for each exercise, with an estimated one-rep max, beyond today's “Best: N reps”.

options.label: Yes, show me options
options.desc: I'd come back with designs to pick from before building.

items.title: Faster week-hours entry
items.why: Tap a number of hours instead of 12 taps of 15 minutes in the week planner.

options.label: Yes, show me options
options.desc: I'd come back with designs to pick from before building.

items.title: Pace in Log activity
items.why: Show pace from distance and minutes for running, cycling, rowing and swimming.

options.label: Yes, show me options
options.desc: I'd come back with designs to pick from before building.

items.title: Repeat yesterday in one tap
items.why: Copy yesterday's meals, or start the last workout again.

options.label: Yes, show me options
options.desc: I'd come back with designs to pick from before building.

items.title: Rest timer per exercise, and supersets
items.why: Set a different rest for a hard lift, or pair two moves back to back.

options.label: Yes, show me options
options.desc: I'd come back with designs to pick from before building.

items.title: Coach or parent summary for teens
items.why: A weekly summary you choose to share, with any red-flag answers at the top. (It's listed as “coming soon” already.)

options.label: Yes, show me options
options.desc: I'd come back with designs to pick from before building.
